<section class="page-intro">
<p class="section-number">Experiment · R package</p>
<h1>OrdinalRegressionViz</h1>
<p class="project-lede">Visual tools for understanding how cumulative ordinal models turn latent evidence into ordered responses.</p>
<div class="article-meta"><span class="status">Published</span><span>Updated 16 Jun 2026</span></div>
</section>
<figure class="project-figure"><img src="../../assets/sdt-distributions-example.png" alt="Latent signal and noise distributions with ordered response thresholds"><figcaption>Latent distributions and the thresholds that convert evidence into response categories.</figcaption></figure>
<section class="project-overview" aria-label="Project overview">
<div><p class="section-number">Question</p><h2>What does the model imply?</h2><p>The package shows how cumulative regression parameters relate to response behavior.</p></div>
<div><p class="section-number">What it provides</p><h2>Plots and measures.</h2><p>It draws latent distributions, ROC curves, posterior predictive checks, and Bayesian forest plots. It also computes d′, criteria, scale ratios, and AUC.</p></div>
<div><p class="section-number">Limit</p><h2>A plot is not a design.</h2><p>A clear figure cannot repair weak data, an unexamined coding choice, or an unsupported causal claim.</p></div>
</section>
